title: Stopping in Los Angeles and sending for a band
summary: On the way to Chicago he stopped in Los Angeles and sent for New Orleans players for a nightclub.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So, where did you go when you left? Los Angeles. Los Angeles. Did you take a band with you?

No. Just taking a vacation, looking around. I was on my way to Chicago. On your way to Chicago? Long way to Chicago. I was on my way to Chicago and stopped in Los Angeles. Did you come by train? Yeah. And soon to find out I was in town, and then the guy opened up a nightclub. Back to Austin. Yeah, the Union Station on Central Avenue. It's a big business. Never had a man in the United. I sent for a band.
Oh, yeah? When you got the job, did you send for a band? It's all right. You can talk. No, you can talk. You can sit down. You can sit back.

Why I sent for a band? I sent for Louie and... Louie? Yeah. Louie went back to New Orleans at the time. Oh. And by the time my telegram got there, he had just left. For Chicago? Mm-hmm. Went with you. So who'd you get? Papa Michael. And who else? I was born in Alfred William Drum and Manuel Mineta. And I was three. Oh, and Wade Whaley. Clarence. You know. Yes, I know.
Piano. Piano. No, piano. He played violin, too. Played trumpet, too. But in your band, where did you play? No, piano. Piano.
No bass. No bass. We skipped that part. Isn't this your pen? Pencil?
